title: Socratic 7x7 Focus Check-in
content:
Purpose: quick, repeatable self-check that surfaces friction, progress, and one small experiment. Inspired by Socratic questioning — seven short prompts repeated each day for a 7-day cadence. Use as scratchpad; not polished.

Format notes (how I use it):
- Each day: answer 7 prompts in 5–10 minutes at morning standup or before deep work.
- Record 1 small experiment (single-action) tied to a KPI.
- End of week: synthesize signals, write micro-retrospective and pick the next experiment.

Weekly KPI snapshot (this week):
- Code commits merged: 8 (target 12)
- Infra incidents affecting latency: 1 (target 0)
- PR review cycle time (avg): 28h (target <24h)
- Focused deep hours: 6 hrs (target 15 hrs)
- Notes: commit volume low due to debugging infra regression. Deep time fractured.

Socratic 7 prompts (abbrev):
1) What am I avoiding?
2) Which friction will give the biggest multiplier if removed?
3) What smallest action can I take now to reduce that friction?
4) What assumption am I testing?
5) What would success look like in 48 hrs?
6) What would success look like in 7 days?
7) One constraint I must honor (time/resource)

Daily entries (scratchy, raw):
Mon 2026-03-02:
1) Avoiding finishing the infra postmortem (it feels like extra doc work).
2) CI flakiness — blocking PR progress across team. Biggest multiplier: reduce flakiness = faster merges.
3) Small action: add deterministic rerun step + quick flaky-test skip flag for failing suite (20m).
4) Assumption: flaky causes are infra timing, not test logic.
5) 48h success: flaky rerun reduces red-green cycles by 30%.
6) 7d success: PR cycle time drops to ~20h.
7) Constraint: can't touch shared CI config after 4pm — coord with infra.
Experiment: add rerun wrapper + metric to track rerun rate.

Tue 2026-03-03:
1) Avoiding writing the short blameless note (still emotional).
2) Biggest friction: context switching between support and feature work.
3) Small action: block two 90-min deep sessions tomorrow and set Slack status.
4) Assumption: blocking calendar will protect deep work.
5) 48h: get 3 focused hours.
6) 7d: finish the failing test triage.
7) Constraint: on-call hours at 3–5pm.
Experiment: deep-block + mute notifications.

Wed 2026-03-04:
1) Avoiding pair debugging with Maya (fear of being slow).
2) Friction multiplier: lack of quick debugging checklist.
3) Action: create 6-step triage checklist in GH comment template (10m).
4) Assumption: a checklist will speed up initial diagnosis.
5) 48h: checklist used once by Maya and saved time.
6) 7d: checklist becomes part of PR template.
7) Constraint: keep checklist <8 steps.
Experiment: add checklist; observe time-to-first-meaningful-signal.

Thu 2026-03-05:
1) Avoiding re-running regression locally (env heavy).
2) Friction multiplier: env friction blocks debugging and learning.
3) Action: add a minimal docker-compose dev profile for core flow (2–3h).
4) Assumption: local env parity will reduce debugging time.
5) 48h: able to repro bug locally once.
6) 7d: dev profile adopted by 2 teammates.
7) Constraint: can't bloat image >300MB.
Experiment: minimal compose profile.

Fri 2026-03-06:
1) Avoiding writing up a short ‘what I learned’ note after pairing.
2) Friction: habit of closing tab without capturing insight.
3) Action: add a 1-sentence capture step to PR merge checklist.
4) Assumption: 1-sentence capture won't feel heavy.
5) 48h: 2 captures added to recent merges.
6) 7d: captures become searchable in GH.
7) Constraint: one sentence, one link max.
Experiment: PR checklist addition.

Sat 2026-03-07 (light day):
1) Avoiding reading backlog threads (decision fatigue).
2) Friction: unread threads hide small but important asks.
3) Action: 15-min triage slot Sunday to tag urgent vs. low priority.
4) Assumption: quick triage reduces async delay.
5) 48h: backlog trimmed a little.
6) 7d: fewer surprises in Monday standup.
7) Constraint: max 15m triage.
Experiment: Sunday triage.

Sun 2026-03-08:
1) Avoiding synthesis of the week (this doc exists to force that).
2) Friction: unsure what signal matters.
3) Action: write the mini-retro (below).
4) Assumption: synthesizing helps next-week planning.
5) 48h: decisions made for next week experiments.
6) 7d: upstreamers see incremental change.
7) Constraint: keep retro <30m.
Experiment: pick 1 experiment to iterate on next week.

Mini-retrospective (synthesis):
- Signal summary: infra regression dominated noise. Quick mitigations (rerun wrapper + triage checklist) gave visible reduction in churn but not enough to hit PR cycle target. Deep hours still below goal; calendar block helped but on-call and urgent triage ate into it.
- What worked: checklist + small env dev profile idea reduced cognitive overhead for debugging. Rerun wrapper prevented repeated re-runs blocking other engineers.
- What didn’t: habit capture (1-sentence) only started; needs nudges. Local repro still brittle for a subset of failures.
- Top 3 priorities next week:
  1) Ship minimal docker-compose dev profile -> target: 2 teammates can repro locally.
  2) Harden rerun metrics and add one alert if rerun rate > 15% for a suite.
  3) Make PR 1-sentence capture mandatory in merge checklist.

Next-week experiment (one):
- Name: dev-profile-and-rerun-observability
- Hypothesis: If I make local repro easy and surface rerun metrics, PR cycle time will drop and on-call interruptions for unknown flakes will reduce by 30% in two weeks.
- Primary metric: PR review cycle time (hours). Secondary: rerun rate %, deep focus hours.
- Small first step (48h): create compose file and a Prometheus counter for reruns.

Open questions / TODO (personal scratch):
- Which flaky tests are legitimately flaky vs. masking infra bugs? Quick audit: pick top 5 failing tests from last 30 days. (TODO: INF-342)
- Can we automate the 1-sentence capture to post to a /team-notes channel? (GH action maybe)
- Follow up with Maya to merge checklist into team template (ask in Monday sync).
- Schedule 2x 90-min deep blocks next Tue/Thu, mark as FOCUS in calendar.

Quick links and traces:
- JIRA INF-342 (regression triage)
- GH PR redwood/ops#1012 (rerun wrapper WIP)
- Slack thread: #eng-weekly-thread (link to on-call chat)

Notes to self:
- Keep experiments atomic. Ship small and measure. If metric moves, double down; if not, stop.
- Guard deep time proactively — calendar-only promises are weak without teammate awareness.
- Emotional note: finishing the postmortem is part of closure; schedule 30-min slot with a coffee to make it less heavy.

End of doc (use as weekly seed).

Revision history (manual):
- 2026-03-05 created initial template + Mon–Wed entries.
- 2026-03-08 added rest of week, micro-retro, next-week experiment.
- 2026-03-12 small edits and linked artifacts.
